##  · D3-q-bench — D3: QEMU virtio-mmio force-legacy blocks real virtio boots; rig evidence pre-R3; testbench edits

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 2

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: Ruled (force-legacy off, rig evidence pre-R3); implemented in b3306141f and 0a676a062 and merged at dc3c8aab1.

### D3 implementer · Question

Event: `405a6ff18b33b0dfa403c2fa5b5ea2fc` · 2026-09-24T20:18:42Z

> **Finding.** This also affects D2/blkd.
> - On this host's QEMU 10.2.2, `qemu-system-riscv64 -M virt -device virtio-mmio,help` reports `force-legacy=<bool> (default: on)`.
> - blkd accepts only virtio-mmio version 2 (servers/blkd/src/virtio.rs: `VERSION: u32 = 2`), and netd will too.
> - tools/testbench/src/qemu.rs never sets it. So no real virtio driver can bring up a device on the bench today. bench-virtio-devices passes because it reads only magic, device ID and config.
> 
> **Proposal.** When a case has [disk] or [net], add `-global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false`, one line in `virtio_devices`. Plus a self-check that the transport reports version 2. No legacy path goes into any driver.
> 
> **Rig evidence before R3.**
> - A D3-owned crate, tests/net, has a launcher (net-rig) that runs as the bundle's first program. It holds the devices, creates the endpoints, budgets and badges, and launches the real netd, ipd and test clients through the R2 stub with named startup blocks.
> - This is the D3 boot evidence: TCP connect and listen, and the three attack cases, with verdicts from the bench peer's connection counts and the in-guest victim.
> - The manifest-driven boot through init stays R3's retained full-server gate.
> - Timer-dependent cases wait for K5: before K5, deadlines fire only when some syscall enters the kernel.
> - Please confirm this is acceptable D3 acceptance evidence.
> 
> **Testbench edits.**
> - A new tools/testbench/src/peer.rs: guestfwd peers with per-address connection counts, and a dial into hostfwd ports.
> - Additive edits:
>   - case.rs: optional [net.peer] and [[net.dial]];
>   - qemu.rs: the guestfwd arguments and force-legacy;
>   - main.rs: mod peer, start and judge the peer;
>   - docs/testbench.md.
> - K5 owns icount, sched_oracle and the post-check hook, and D3 does not touch them. If K5's hook lands first, the peer judgment uses it.
> - **Coordination needed** on the order of the case.rs, qemu.rs and main.rs edits.
